kira (eng-runtime): Ran a focused replay harness this morning to reproduce the perf regression on prefill-dominant long-context workloads. Wanted to dump what I observed and get ideas before digging deeper.

kira (eng-runtime): Setup: replay harness with preserved inter-arrival times, configs: 16xA100, sequence mix skewed to 8%<=8k tokens (prefill-heavy), concurrency=120, synthetic clients = replayer v2. Command: `./harness/replay --trace prefill-heavy.json --concurrency 120 --preserve-arrival`

kira (eng-runtime): Key things I saw:
- kernel selector switched from "matmul_fused_fast" to "matmul_generic" for a subset of layers under load (likely due to workspace memory checks).
- batching heuristics collapsed into tiny batches during prefill phase then grew for generation, causing KV cache churn.
- KV cache evictions: saw repeated KV rebuilds for 2% of requests, correlated with batch boundary changes.

kira (eng-runtime): Sample logs (filtered):
```
[2026-03-10T09:12:03Z] req=0x7f3a1 select_kernel: layer=6 chosen=matmul_generic reason=workspace_insufficient
[2026-03-10T09:12:03Z] req=0x7f3a1 batcher: batch_size=3 prefill_ratio=0.93 dynamic_shrink=true
[2026-03-10T09:12:03Z] kvcache: miss_rebuild=true key_len=8192 alloc_retry=1
[2026-03-10T09:12:05Z] perf: latency_p95=842ms p99=1.9s tokens/s=540
```

sam (perf): Oof. Two quick angles: (1) kernel fallback — do we have recent changes to workspace sizing or alloc policy? (2) batching — prefill_ratio metric looks high; the batcher maybe trying to minimize latency for short-gen tokens and accidentally breaking prefill locality.

maria (ml-infra): I pushed a micro-change last week to the kernel allocator that tightened the transient workspace cap when GPU memory fragmentation > 60%. Could be related. I can revert for a canary.

noah (devex): For apples-to-apples: make sure both baseline and PR runs use identical sequence-length distribution and client arrival jitter. In past we saw 10% difference from arrival jitter alone. Use `--preserve-arrival --seed=42` to keep deterministic.

ashley (sre): Also confirm host-side NUMA pinning + cudaMallocTrim behavior. On dense prefill we sometimes hit allocator slow paths. Did you collect `nvprof` traces or `nvidia-smi` snapshots?

kira (eng-runtime): I grabbed perf traces and a couple flamegraphs. Uploading links: <flame/1718456723/main.svg> and <flame/1718456723/branch.svg> (private). Quick diffs: branch had extra stack frames in `allocator::try_trim` and `kv_cache::rebuild_loop`.

sam (perf): Suggestion: Split benchmark into two phases in the harness: (A) prefill-only (send only context blocks, record kernel choices and KV touches), (B) generation-only starting from cached KV state. That isolates prefill-induced regressions vs generation latency.

kira (eng-runtime): Good idea. I added flags `--phase prefill|generate|both` and re-ran. Prefill-only run shows 30% slower kernel runtime in branch vs main for matmul layers 4-8. Generation-only looks comparable if starting from warmed KV. So problem is in prefill path.

maria (ml-infra): If kernel selection falls back because of ephemeral workspace, maybe increase the workspace budget for prefill path. We could also make selector prefer quantized kernels when sequence_length>4096.

noah (devex): Another batching heuristic: modify dynamic_batcher to consider "prefill_affinity": keep requests with >80% prefill in the same batch if possible to maximize KV cache share. Rough patch I used before: `if prefill_ratio >= 0.8 and batch.size < max_batch: prefer_join()`

ashley (sre): We must be careful — preferring affinity can increase head-of-line blocking. Add a per-request timeout so we don't increase P99. Default timeout=25ms.

kira (eng-runtime): I instrumented KV cache statistics: per-shard hit_rate during prefill was 0.88 on main, 0.71 on branch. Rebuild_count on branch = 134 in 10k requests, main = 12. So it's not just kernel perf, KV behavior matters.

sam (perf): For apples-to-apples baseline, capture: a) gpu mem fragmentation (via `nvidia-smi --query`), b) free bytes timeline, c) batch size distribution histogram, d) per-layer kernel chosen counts. Store as artifact for comparison.

kira (eng-runtime): I uploaded artifacts to the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/rep/1718456723/{kernel_counts.json, batch_hist.csv, kv_stats.json, flame_main.svg, flame_branch.svg}

maria (ml-infra): Next steps I propose:
- revert my workspace cap tweak in a canary to confirm root cause
- add a guard in the kernel selector: prefer `matmul_fused_fast` when workspace difference < 10% to avoid oscillation under transient fragmentation
- add a batcher heuristic flag `--prefer_prefill_affinity` default false

noah (devex): I'll update the replay harness docs to include the two-phase mode and the recommended env flags for deterministic runs.

ashley (sre): I'll run a controlled stress with NUMA pinning and record allocator events. If we reproduce, we should consider bumping the default small-allocation GPU pool size.

deploy-bot: Deployed branch perf-canary to perf-cluster-a at 2026-03-10T12:04:13Z (id=canary-1718456723).

kira (eng-runtime): Action items summary: maria revert/change kernel allocator; sam add artifact checklist and per-layer counts; noah update docs and seed; ashley run allocator stress; I’ll iterate on batcher affinity patch and re-run replay.

sam (perf): Also schedule an apples-to-apples comparison job that runs baseline and branch back-to-back with identical harness seeds and stores diff metrics (p95, p99, kv_rebuilds, kernel_change_count). I can own the dashboard.

kira (eng-runtime): Thanks all. Will post CSV diffs and next run results here once the canary is up. :raised_hands:
